subject: Bridge lane latency surge, stabilization steps, and roadmap asks
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-03-12T09:43:00-07:00
Subject: Bridge lane latency surge — immediate triage request

Team,

Observed a sharp p95 latency jump and sustained throughput drop for the bridge routing lane serving HelixPay (model: redwood-gen-2) starting ~02:30 UTC this morning. Metrics: p95 from ~240ms -> ~1.2s; provisioned QPS steady but completion latency and a ~1.6% error-rate increase. Affected routes are high-fanout (many short prompts with repeated prefixes).

I attached a trimmed logs bundle (logs_20290312.zip) and a short perf snapshot in Drive. Immediate asks:
- Karthik / SRE: can you triage memory/kv-cache pressure and node-level evictions? I flagged a potential correlation with a non-user-facing deploy at ~02:30 UTC.
- Marissa / Product: we need short-term options to protect the customer (fallback model / throttles / prefix cache).
- Kimberly / CS: please prepare a holding message for HelixPay and ask for consent to apply temporary throttles during their peak window if needed.

Ideal immediate mitigation = one of the following (prioritized):
1) switch HelixPay traffic to a compatible, lower-latency model variant (gen-2-q4) for 30 mins while we stabilize;
2) enable conservative prefix caching on the bridge lane (300s TTL) to catch repeated prefixes;
3) short, targeted throttle on HelixPay fanout (20-30%) during sharp spikes.

I will be on the 10:30 sync to walk through the logs.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: logs_20290312.zip
Link: https://drive.redwood.internal/drive/bridgesurge/triage-20290312

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-03-12T09:57:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Bridge lane latency surge — immediate triage request

Rafael — thanks for the heads up and the logs. Quick triage notes after an initial pass:
- We see KV cache churn and elevated mem pressure on the bridge pod group coincident with the 02:30 UTC deploy. Several shard leaders reported >85% mem util and started evicting prefixes aggressively.
- There are a handful of nodes with an unusual token fanout amplification — likely due to repeated prefix requests from HelixPay endpoints.

Short-term mitigations I can apply immediately if you approve:
- Restart warm pool for the affected bridge group to rehydrate KV cache (estimated 30s rolling restarts, low impact).
- Flip routing to allow model-variant fallback (gen-2-q4) for HelixPay for a rolling 15–30 minute window. Latency delta expected: p95 reduction from ~1.2s -> ~300–500ms on fallback model in our bench.
- Apply an upstream soft-throttle filter (20%) on HelixPay's connection to reduce extreme fanout spikes.

Risks: model-variant fallback will reduce per-request cost efficiency for that tenant and may slightly change tokenization behavior. Cache TTL changes are low risk.

I recommend we: (A) restart warm pool now, (B) enable prefix caching with 300s TTL on bridge lane, and (C) standby to flip fallback if latency doesn't drop within 10–15m.

If everyone is ok I will run (A) and (B) now and draft the customer note for Kimberly.

—Karthik
Director, SRE

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-03-12T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Bridge lane latency surge — product tradeoffs and roadmap ask

Thanks — quick product perspective.

Short-term: agree with Karthik's mitigation path. Please keep me posted on measured p95 after warm-pool restart and after prefix caching. We should choose fallback only if caching + restart don't bring p95 below ~500ms.

Roadmap ask (ask to Eng & PM):
- Scope an "adaptive prefix cache" story: TTL heuristics + per-tenant cache sizing (Q2 sprint). This would mitigate fanout-heavy tenants without manual intervention.
- Scope a low-latency fallback policy feature (configurable per-route) so AE/CS can toggle fallback models without an ops-runbook.

Please provide:
- Eng estimate (story points) and expected latency improvement (bench) for both items by 2029-03-20 so we can commit in next planning.

I've attached a short draft customer note (draft_customer_note_v1.md) that Kimberly can use as a starting point.

Marissa Cole
Head of Product, Redwood Inference

From: Samir Shah <samir@helixpay.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: HelixPay SRE <sre@helixpay.com>
Date: 2029-03-12T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Bridge lane latency surge — immediate triage request

Rafael / Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick flag. This window is painful for us — we see increased checkout timeouts for a subset of customers between 12:00–14:00 UTC. Two asks from HelixPay:
1) please provide a timeline summary of what changed at 02:30 UTC and what you're doing to stabilize (p95 improvement numbers would help).
2) we will likely request credit for SLA impact if our end metrics continue to degrade; please advise next steps.

We can also temporarily decrease fanout from our side if you can confirm the most aggressive endpoints to throttle — we want to apply the least disruptive throttles possible.

Samir Shah
Head of Platform, HelixPay

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Samir Shah <samir@helixpay.com>, HelixPay SRE <sre@helixpay.com>
Date: 2029-03-14T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-mortem-lite & action items — Bridge surge (HelixPay)

Folks — summary and concrete next steps after the past 48 hours:

What we saw:
- 2029-03-12 02:30 UTC: internal deploy triggered higher mem pressure on bridge pod group; KV cache churn + prefix evictions correlated with p95 increase (240ms -> ~1.2s).
- Fanout-heavy requests from HelixPay amplified the impact.

Immediate mitigations applied (3/12):
- Warm-pool restart and KV-cache prefill executed (Karthik) — p95 improved to ~350–500ms within 12 minutes.
- Enabled prefix caching with 300s TTL on the bridge lane — reduced repeated-request load by ~28%.
- Enabled model-variant fallback route for HelixPay during peak windows; applied a temporary soft-throttle (20%) for the highest-fanout endpoints (Grace coordinated).
- Customer note sent and collaboration with HelixPay SRE confirmed temporary upstream throttling for two endpoints.

Commitments / roadmap asks:
- Marissa/Product to scope adaptive prefix cache and per-tenant cache sizing by 2029-03-20 (owner: Marissa).
- Eng to estimate effort for a configurable per-route fallback toggle and the gen-2-q4 validation run (owner: Karthik). Target: prototype in 2 weeks, rollout in next cadence if tests pass.
- CS to produce an SLA impact calc and credit proposal (owner: Kimberly).

Action items (owners & due dates):
- Karthik: confirm warm-pool mitigation metrics and provide bench numbers for gen-2-q4 by 2029-03-16.
- Marissa: product spec draft for adaptive prefix cache by 2029-03-20.
- Kimberly: finalize customer communication and SLA credit approach by 2029-03-15.
- Rafael/Grace: coordinate with HelixPay on throttle windows and follow-ups; update JIRA-INC-4721 with timeline and attachments.

Attachments: draft_customer_note_v1.md, kv_cache_warmup_plan.pdf, logs_20290312.zip
Link: JIRA-INC-4721

Thanks all — please hit reply with any clarifying items or if timelines need adjustment.

Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
